transcript.text: Alright, everyone. We've got the medical-device housing run scheduled for Thursday, and I understand our virgin polymer supply isn't sufficient to complete the planned batch on its own. I also understand there's a lot of reclaimed polymer pellets available in the materials cage that hasn't been authorized for this product yet. Before I make any authorization decision, I need quality and environmental compliance to weigh in. Could both of you please state your exact requirements and confirm which controls you'll complete before Thursday's run? Once I have both responses on the record, I'll settle the authorization and control plan.

I also confirmed that the first 50 molded housings must receive FTIR identity testing, but the lab result has not yet been attached to the production traveler.

transcript.text: My review of the supplier's revised safety data sheet — received late yesterday and not yet entered in the plant's chemical register — classifies the reclaimed lot's additive residue as regulated process waste. That means we need labeled segregated storage and a hazardous-waste manifest for any discarded pellets or purge material. I can complete the chemical-register entry, storage setup, and manifest procedures before Thursday, and I will provide environmental-compliance sign-off once those controls are complete.
